Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly velocity snapshot — QBR readiness and targeted asks

Team — sending a compact readout ahead of Friday’s QBR dry run. TL;DR: overall momentum looks good; three items where I need quick leadership input or resourcing.

Wins:
- Acme pilot passed performance acceptance (99.2% uptime for 7-day window) — Sophie at Acme confirmed demo success.
- Dedicated capacity rollout for two enterprise pilots completed (no regressions reported).
- New prompt-eval harness reduced false-positive rerank rate by ~12% in staging.

Risks / concerns:
1) Procurement hold for Acme: they requested SOC scope clarification and a signature on our revised DPA before they sign the Dedicated contract. Point person: Sophie at Acme (external).
2) Latency regression reported on mid-size sequences into region-us-east-1 during peak; root-cause points to batching config shift after optimizer deploy last week. Impacted customers: two pilots (Acme + internal sandbox).
3) QBR deck still missing one slide: alignment on forecasted committed capacity vs planned burst. Need accurate numbers for finance.

Asks (actionable):
- Laura: can you approve doing a one-time 10% burst credit for Acme to honor their demo SLA while procurement completes? (Decision required by EOD Thu)
- Karthik: please assign an infra engineer to a 6-hour incident review and rollback window if we don’t land the performance fix by Thu 18:00 PT. Dev option: Dev Patel is available but will need a PM/leader sign-off for re-prioritization.
- Marissa: can you confirm CS will run the customer QBR prep call Thursday (agenda + pre-read)? I’ll attach the draft deck.

Attachments: QBR-prefix-deck-v1.pdf (slides), customer-risk-log-20270505.csv (raw issue list).

Next steps: I’ll run the dry-run Friday 10:00 PT with Laura + Karthik + Marissa — please confirm availability.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the crisp summary, Jasmine. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I confirm the burst request:

1) For the one-time 10% burst credit: what's the $ impact estimate (ballpark) and will we need a contract amendment? Procurement at Acme specifically called out DPA + signature timing, not credits; want to understand if this becomes a precedent.

2) On the latency regression: can you confirm whether the optimizer deploy is a config-only change (reversible) or requires a model-side rollback? If reversible, I’m comfortable approving the incident window for Dev to investigate.

I can be on the dry-run Friday 10:00 PT.

On the deck: I want a short slide that shows committed capacity (monthly reserved GPU hours) vs typical observed peak for the pilot. If you can drop that in by EOD Thu, I’ll approve.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Laura — answers inline and updated attachments attached.

1) Burst credit impact: ballpark $3.5k (one-off for May). We can do this without a contract amendment; treat as a goodwill credit on the first invoice while DPA is in signature queue. I’ll flag in the invoice notes. If approved, Finance will require a quick PMR ticket to record.

2) Latency regression: the optimizer change was a runtime/batching heuristic tweak (config-only) that is reversible. Dev Patel can run a rollback and validate in the canary pool; estimated 4–6 hours to complete and validate.

3) Deck slide: added 'Committed vs Observed Capacity' slide (see QBR-prefix-deck-v1.pdf). Also attached customer-risk-log-20270505.csv with the Acme procurement item highlighted.

Availability: I confirm Fri 10:00 PT for the dry-run.

Thanks,
Jasmine
